result.summary: This pull request implements the BIP 54 (Consensus Cleanup) consensus validation rules. The rules address known consensus weaknesses: enforcing a 2-hour grace period on difficulty adjustment timestamps (timewarp fix), preventing negative difficulty retarget intervals (Murch-Zawy rule), requiring coinbase locktime to match block height minus one, prohibiting 64-byte transactions (CVE-2017-12842 Merkle tree vulnerability), and capping legacy non-witness signature operations to 2,500. The rules are deployed via versionbits and configured as always active on regtest, while left without mainnet activation.
result.problem: Bitcoin consensus currently permits several edge-case attacks and resource-exhaustion vectors, including timewarp difficulty manipulation, Merkle tree inner-node collision with 64-byte transactions, and excessive legacy sigops leading to quadratic or prolonged block validation delays.

resolved_concerns: fjahr noted the miner did not enforce the Murch-Zawy rule; this was extracted and merged in #35949 before rebasing.
ariard asked about sigops counting asymmetry for empty vs non-empty CHECKMULTISIG; darosior clarified it aligns with existing BIP 16 accounting.

polespinasa questioned flagging non-standard sigops as TX_CONSENSUS in validation errors; darosior explained the rationale regarding disconnect policy and Inquisition parity, documenting it in commit messages.
p2p_segwit functional test was updated to use BIP 54 compliant blocks prior to consensus rule enforcement.

result.card: This PR implements the consensus validation rules proposed in BIP 54 (Consensus Cleanup), activating them on regtest while leaving mainnet activation for future consideration. It resolves known security and consensus flaws: timewarp attacks, negative difficulty adjustment periods, Merkle tree malleability via 64-byte transactions (CVE-2017-12842), and block validation CPU DoS from excessive legacy sigops. Over 95% of the additions consist of unit tests, functional tests, and test vectors previously vetted on Bitcoin Inquisition. Review state is active and positive with seven Concept ACKs from contributors and maintainers, and all review points have been addressed.
